On an industrial search-ad dataset, with prefixes prepared, query-level HR@100 rises by 3.83 percentage points and mean online latency falls 38.9% versus all-online 0.5B; HR@100 is comparable to all-online 7B at 57.7% lower online latency. A production A/B experiment lasting over a month reports about 10% lower inference cost than uniformly using the expensive tier, with minimal latency impact and no observed quality regression so far. Public MovieLens and Amazon experiments show that extra LLM computation can instead harm sparse-history users. The practical lesson for ranking compute allocation is to measure benefit by user segment and domain before escalation, rather than treating more inference as uniformly helpful. |
